definition: A position closed by force because its margin ran out.
boundaries: On perps it is the venue closing at the mark price, visible as public flow; on FX and CFDs it is the broker's stop-out on one account, private; on futures a margin call, private.
recognition: A cascade of perp liquidations reads as forced flow, not opinion.

class_meanings.fx: The broker's stop-out of one account: private, never market data.
class_meanings.metal: The broker's stop-out of one account: private.
class_meanings.index_cfd: The broker's stop-out of one account: private.
class_meanings.commodity_cfd: The broker's stop-out of one account: private.
class_meanings.stock_cfd: The broker's stop-out of one account: private.
class_meanings.future: A margin call between a trader and the clearing firm: private.
class_meanings.perp: The venue closes the position at the mark price; the order is public flow.

sources.quote: A liquidation event occurs when a trader's positions move against them
